title: Cold rebuild: Which editor will git open?
summary: Rebuild Which editor will git open? from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Which editor will git open?** in *nano on servers*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: Why is nano often the right choice when you write instructions for a colleague on a production server?
options: What they type goes straight into the file and the exit keys are printed on screen, so a nervous typist cannot get stuck in a mode
It is faster than vim for every task
It is installed on every container image
steps.explain: nano is modeless and self-documenting. It is not everywhere (minimal images often have only `vi`, or nothing), which is why you learn vi too.
